s: Which one of the following correctly describes the SENSEX?
o: A dollar-linked index of 30 NSE stocks
A BSE index of 20 carbon-efficient companies
An NSE index of 50 stocks from 13 sectors calculated on the basis of full market capitalisation
A BSE index of 30 blue-chip stocks calculated on the basis of free-float market capitalisation
x: SENSEX comprises 30 blue-chip stocks listed on the BSE and is calculated using the free-float market capitalisation method.
tq: Split the options by exchange, number of stocks and calculation method.
sec: Stock indices - exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

s:
With reference to the NIFTY 50, consider the following statements:
1. It consists of 50 stocks representing 13 sectors.
2. It is based on free-float market capitalisation.
3. It was launched in 1996.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: NIFTY 50 consists of 50 stocks from 13 sectors, uses free-float market capitalisation and was launched in 1996.
tq: Use the coded combination to verify the exchange, method and launch year together.
sec: Stock indices - exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

s: The base year and base value of the SENSEX are respectively:
x: The SENSEX has 1978–79 as its base year and a base value of 100.
tq: Match the two numerical attributes instead of confusing them with NIFTY figures.
sec: Stock indices - exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

s: NIFTY 50 has which of the following as its base date and base value?
x: NIFTY 50 uses 3 November 1995 as its base date and 1,000 as its base value.
tq: Separate the base date from the launch date and compare the paired figures.
sec: Stock indices - exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: DOLLEX-30 is a BSE dollar-linked version of the Sensex and was launched on 25 July 2001.
tq: Start from the distinctive dollar-linked description and eliminate exchange and date swaps.
sec: Stock indices - exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

s: GREENEX is associated with which one of the following combinations?
x: GREENEX is a BSE index comprising 20 stocks and uses carbon-efficiency weighting.
tq: Use the uncommon number and environmental weighting as the identification clues.
sec: Stock indices - exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

s: Which one of the following is NOT a share-price index?
x: Moody’s is a ratings agency, not a share-price index. SENSEX, NIFTY 50 and DOLLEX-30 are market indices.
tq: Find the odd institutional category rather than focusing only on familiar financial names.
sec: Stock indices - exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

s: NIFTY is managed by which institution?
o: Indian Index Services and Products, now NSE Indices Ltd.
Securities and Exchange Board of India
x: NIFTY is managed by IISL, now known as NSE Indices Ltd., a subsidiary of NSE.
tq: Apply the ‘who manages it?’ test to distinguish an index provider from its regulator.
sec: Stock indices - exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

s: After the addition of 11 sectoral indices, the number of indices associated with NSE was stated to have reached:
x: The addition of 11 sectoral indices took the total number of NSE indices to 34.
tq: Use the stated addition and total, avoiding confusion with the NIFTY 50 stock count.
sec: Stock indices - exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

s: India’s position in global market capitalisation, after being overtaken by South Korea, was:
x: India fell to seventh position in global market capitalisation after being overtaken by South Korea.
tq: Distinguish a country ranking from an index ranking.
sec: Stock indices - exchange, number of stocks, method, launch

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the BSE is correct?
o: It became a national exchange in 1957.
It was established in Mumbai in 1992 by financial institutions.
It was first recognised under the SCRA on 31 August 1957.
It was India’s first international exchange in 2016.
x: BSE received its first recognition under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act on 31 August 1957.
tq: Separate the recognition date from the establishment and national-exchange dates.

s: The BSE was promoted by the:
o: Native Share and Stock Brokers’ Association
x: The BSE was promoted by the Native Share and Stock Brokers’ Association.
tq: Identify the promoter rather than the committee associated with NSE.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the National Stock Exchange?
o: Established in 1992 at Mumbai and set up by financial institutions on the advice of the Pherwani Committee
Established in 1875 at Mumbai by the Native Share and Stock Brokers’ Association
Established in 2016 at GIFT City as India’s first international exchange
Established in 2008 at Mumbai as MCX-SX
x: NSE was established in 1992 at Mumbai and was set up by financial institutions following the Pherwani Committee’s advice.
tq: Use the promoter and committee pairing to distinguish NSE from BSE and MSE.

s: Which one of the following exchanges was initially known as MCX-SX and was renamed in 2015?
x: The Metropolitan Stock Exchange began in Mumbai in 2008 as MCX-SX and was renamed in 2015.
tq: Test the former-name and renaming-year pair directly.

s: India INX, established on 30 December 2016, is located at:
x: India INX is located at GIFT City IFSC and was India’s first international exchange.
tq: Link the exchange with its distinctive location and international status.

s: Which institution regulates exchanges located in an International Financial Services Centre?
x: Exchanges in an IFSC are regulated by the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA).
tq: Use the institutional-jurisdiction clue: IFSC exchanges correspond to IFSCA.

s: NSEIX Global Access enables Indian investors to:
o: Buy shares exclusively in commodity exchanges
x: NSEIX Global Access enables Indians to buy United States stocks.
tq: Translate the facility’s name and purpose into the permitted investor activity.

s: Which of the following belongs exclusively to the primary market?
o: Sale of shares between two investors on an exchange
Trading of existing securities on a stock exchange
Trading in gilt-edged securities already issued
x: An IPO is a new issue in the primary market. Trading in existing securities belongs to the secondary market.
tq: Discriminate between new issue transactions and resale of existing securities.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a primary-market transaction, money goes to the issuer.
2. Stock-exchange trading of existing securities is part of the secondary market.
3. Rights issues and private placements are primary-market transactions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Primary-market issues include IPOs, FPOs, rights issues and private placements, with funds going to the issuer. Trading existing securities is secondary-market activity.
tq: Classify each transaction by whether it creates a new issue or transfers an existing security.

s: In an IPO, the proceeds from an offer for sale generally go to:
x: In an offer for sale, existing owners sell their holdings and receive the proceeds; proceeds from a fresh issue go to the firm.
tq: Separate the recipient of OFS proceeds from the recipient of fresh-issue proceeds.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the reported share of promoters, private-equity and venture-capital investors in OFS proceeds in calendar year 2026 up to early July?
x: Promoters, PE and VC investors accounted for 84% of OFS proceeds, or ₹10,696 crore, in the stated period.
tq: Check the percentage and rupee amount as a pair, not independently.

s: India’s share of global IPO listings was approximately:
x: India accounted for approximately 30% of global IPO listings and led the world in the number of IPO issues.
tq: Use the approximate share while rejecting the rounded extreme alternatives.

s: A market participant who expects stock prices to decline is known as a:
x: A bear expects prices to fall, whereas a bull expects prices to rise.
tq: Directly distinguish the paired market expectations.

s: A person who buys IPO shares mainly to sell them quickly after listing is called a:
x: A stag applies for IPO shares with the intention of selling them soon after listing.
tq: Match the specialised IPO term with its distinctive behaviour.

s: Short selling involves:
o: Selling borrowed shares and buying them back later at a lower price
Buying shares and holding them until maturity
Exchanging fixed-rate debt for floating-rate debt
Issuing new shares below their face value
x: In short selling, borrowed shares are sold first and are bought back later, ideally at a lower price.
tq: Follow the transaction sequence—borrow, sell, buy back—to identify the term.

s: A beta of 1 for a stock indicates that the stock generally:
o: Has no relation to market volatility
Moves exactly opposite to the market
x: Beta measures a stock’s volatility relative to the market; beta 1 indicates movement with the market.
tq: Use the reference value of one to interpret relative volatility.

s: A circuit breaker in a securities market is intended to:
o: Halt trading when an index or stock moves beyond prescribed limits
x: A circuit breaker temporarily halts trading when the movement in an index or stock exceeds specified limits.
tq: Identify the market-stabilisation function rather than an investor-return function.

s: Sweat equity shares are issued to employees or directors mainly in consideration of:
o: A fall in the company’s share price
x: Sweat equity is issued to employees or directors for know-how or services, often at a discount.
tq: Connect the instrument with non-cash contribution by insiders.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the two depositories in India?
o: NSDL was the first depository, while CDSL was promoted by BSE
CDSL was the first depository, while NSDL was promoted by BSE
Both were established as commodity exchanges
NSDL and CDSL are stock indices rather than depositories
x: NSDL was the first depository and is located in Mumbai; CDSL was promoted by BSE. Depositories hold securities in dematerialised form.
tq: Use the first-mover and promoter clues to separate NSDL from CDSL.

s: NSDL, the first depository in India, commenced operations on:
x: NSDL was the first Indian depository and commenced operations on 6 November 1996.
tq: Distinguish the depository date from the launch dates of market indices and exchanges.

s: The standard securities settlement cycle referred to as T+1 means settlement takes place:
o: Five trading days after the transaction
One trading day after the transaction
On the same calendar day only
x: T+1 denotes settlement one trading day after the transaction. Optional same-day T+0 settlement is also available.
tq: Decode the letter-number notation by treating T as the transaction day.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding shareholders and debenture-holders?
o: Shareholders are creditors, while debenture-holders are residual owners
Shareholders are owners, while debenture-holders are creditors paid before shareholders
Debenture-holders receive dividends only after shareholders
Both have an identical residual claim on company assets
x: Shareholders are owners with a residual claim and possible dividends. Debenture or bondholders are creditors and are paid before shareholders.
tq: Compare ownership, creditor status and priority of payment.

s: Convertible bonds or debentures are called hybrid instruments because they combine features of:
x: Convertible bonds or debentures are debt instruments that may carry an equity-conversion feature, making them hybrids of debt and equity.
tq: Identify the two financial-claim categories combined in the instrument.

s: Mutual fund units are generally priced with reference to:
o: The face value of the fund manager’s shares
x: Mutual funds pool investors’ money and their units are priced with reference to Net Asset Value (NAV).
tq: Match the pooled-investment product with its standard valuation term.

s: An arbitrage fund is required by SEBI to maintain at least what proportion in equity?
x: Arbitrage funds must maintain at least 65% of their investments in equity.
tq: Use the statutory threshold rather than confusing it with common equity-fund proportions.

s: Crowdfunding refers to:
o: Raising small sums from many people through an online platform
Borrowing exclusively from one commercial bank
Issuing government bonds only to foreign investors
x: Crowdfunding raises small amounts from a large number of people, generally through online platforms.
tq: Identify the many-small-contributors structure of the financing method.

s: Asset tokenisation is best described as:
o: Digital representation of ownership or claims on a programmable ledger
Physical printing of all securities certificates
Conversion of equity into only gold holdings
x: Asset tokenisation digitally represents ownership or claims such as bonds, fund units and receivables on a programmable ledger.
tq: Translate the technology term into its underlying ownership-and-ledger function.

s: Which of the following is a stated potential benefit of asset tokenisation?
o: Faster settlement and pledgeable assets that may improve MSME credit
Restriction of all assets to physical certificates
Removal of the need for any ownership record
x: Asset tokenisation can enable faster settlement, make assets pledgeable and improve access to credit for MSMEs.
tq: Select the option expressing practical financial effects rather than an absolute claim.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes futures from options?
o: Futures create an obligation, whereas options provide a right but not an obligation
Futures provide only a right, whereas options create an obligation
Both futures and options create only rights
Neither futures nor options relates to a future transaction
x: A futures contract creates an obligation to buy or sell at a fixed future price. An option gives the holder a right, but not an obligation.
tq: Focus on the decisive distinction between obligation and right.

s: A call option and a put option respectively provide the right to:
o: Exchange fixed and floating interest only
x: A call option gives the right to buy, while a put option gives the right to sell.
tq: Pair each option name with its action and avoid reversing the two.

s: Swaps generally involve:
o: Exchange of cash flows, such as fixed interest for floating interest
Issue of shares only to employees
Sale of borrowed shares followed by repurchase
Trading of only newly issued securities
x: Swaps involve exchanging cash flows; a common example is exchanging fixed-rate interest payments for floating-rate payments.
tq: Identify the cash-flow exchange rather than a transfer of ownership.

s: Which one of the following statements about commodity derivatives in India is correct?
o: Commodity derivatives are regulated exclusively by IFSCA.
The Forward Markets Commission merged into SEBI in 2015.
The Forward Markets Commission became a part of RBI in 1998.
The merger took place in 2022 under the Companies Act.
x: The Forward Markets Commission merged with SEBI in 2015, bringing commodity derivatives under SEBI’s regulatory framework.
tq: Use the regulator and year together to catch institutional swaps.

s: NCDEX RAINMUMBAI is associated with India’s first:
x: NCDEX RAINMUMBAI is India’s first weather derivative.
tq: Match the specialised product name with its unusual derivative category.

s: Which one of the following is associated with NSE in the derivatives market?
x: NSE offers electricity futures among the derivatives products identified.
tq: Link the exchange with the specific product rather than a neighbouring financial instrument.

s: Derivatives in India are regulated by SEBI under the:
x: SEBI regulates derivatives under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.
tq: Check the regulator–statute combination instead of choosing a broadly related law.

s: Which committees are associated with the design and development of India’s futures and options market?
o: L.C. Gupta Committee and J.R. Varma Committee
x: The L.C. Gupta Committee was associated with the 1998 framework and the J.R. Varma Committee with the 2002 development of the F&O market.
tq: Use the two committee names as a pair and reject committees from unrelated sectors.

s: Which statement regarding India’s options market is correct?
o: It is among the world’s largest by number of contracts, but SEBI found that nine out of ten option traders lost money.
It is among the world’s smallest markets, and almost all traders made profits.
It is restricted to institutional investors and has no retail participation.
It permits expiry on every day of the week without limitation.
x: India’s options market is among the largest by contracts, while SEBI found that nine out of ten option traders lost money.
tq: Combine the market-size fact with the investor-outcome fact and reject extreme reversals.

s: Under the stated expiry-day rule, options expiry may be scheduled only on:
x: The stated rule limits options expiry days to Tuesday or Thursday.
tq: Discriminate between adjacent weekdays in a close-date factual question.

s: Under the changes announced in Budget 2026–27, the securities transaction tax on futures was increased from:
x: Budget 2026–27 raised the STT on futures from 0.02% to 0.05%.
tq: Read the old and new rates as a directional pair rather than confusing them with options rates.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the revised STT rates on options under Budget 2026–27?
x: The options premium rate was raised to 0.10%, while the exercise rate was raised to 0.15%.
tq: Keep the premium and exercise components in their correct order.

s: Following the Budget 2026–27 increase in STT, the Nifty recorded a fall of:
x: The Nifty fell by 1.96% following the stated increase in STT.
tq: Select the exact reported percentage rather than rounding the market movement.

s: In the book-building process of an Initial Public Offering (IPO), which one of the following correctly describes the method of price discovery?
o: The face value of the share becomes the final issue price irrespective of demand
The stock exchange determines the price after listing
The issuer fixes a single price before receiving any investor bids
Investors bid within a price band, and the final issue price is determined from the bids received
x: In book building, investors submit bids within a price band extending from the floor price to the cap price. The final IPO price is determined on the basis of the bids received.
tq: Identify the precise process description and reject fixed-price alternatives.
sec: IPO process - book building, anchors, ASBA, SME IPO, listing

s: The term ‘Greenshoe option’ in an IPO refers to the facility by which:
o: Retail investors can purchase shares at a discount after listing
The stock exchange can cancel an under-subscribed issue
Anchor investors can transfer their locked-in shares before listing
The issuer can sell additional shares when demand for the issue is high
x: The Greenshoe option permits the issuer to sell extra shares when demand for the IPO is high. It is associated with managing additional demand in the issue.
tq: Use the distinctive function of the named IPO facility to eliminate nearby but incorrect functions.
sec: IPO process - book building, anchors, ASBA, SME IPO, listing

s:
With reference to anchor investors in an IPO, consider the following statements:
1. They are Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs).
2. They bid before the issue opens for general subscription.
3. Their investment is subject to a lock-in.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Anchor investors are QIBs who bid before the issue opens for general subscription, and their investment is subject to a lock-in. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
tq: Check the institutional identity, timing and restriction together before selecting the complete combination.
sec: IPO process - book building, anchors, ASBA, SME IPO, listing

s: Under the ASBA mechanism for an IPO, the application money:
o: Remains blocked in the investor’s bank account until allotment
Is deposited with the stock exchange until listing
Is converted into a fixed deposit until the issue closes
Is immediately transferred to the issuing company upon submission of the application
x: Under ASBA, the application money remains blocked in the investor’s bank account until the allotment process. The amount is debited in accordance with the shares allotted.
tq: Distinguish blocking of funds from immediate transfer or payment.
sec: IPO process - book building, anchors, ASBA, SME IPO, listing

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in the context of SME IPOs?

1. BSE SME — SME platform
2. NSE Emerge — SME platform
3. ASBA — Separate SME listing platform
x: BSE SME and NSE Emerge are separate platforms on which SME IPOs are listed. ASBA is an IPO application mechanism, not an SME listing platform.
tq: Separate the listing platforms from the application mechanism before choosing the combination.
sec: IPO process - book building, anchors, ASBA, SME IPO, listing

s: SME IPOs in India are generally listed on:
o: BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty only
India INX and the gilt-edged market
x: SME IPOs are listed on dedicated SME platforms, notably BSE SME and NSE Emerge. NSDL and CDSL are depositories rather than listing platforms.
tq: Identify the dedicated market platforms and distinguish them from indices and depositories.
sec: IPO process - book building, anchors, ASBA, SME IPO, listing

s: An SME IPO is required to be listed within which period from the closing of the issue?
x: SME IPOs are listed within T+3 days of the closing of the issue. Here, T denotes the issue-closing day.
tq: Compare the closely spaced settlement-time options and retain the stated T-plus period.
sec: IPO process - book building, anchors, ASBA, SME IPO, listing

s: For very large companies, the minimum portion offered to the public in an IPO may be reduced to:
x: The public offer portion for very large companies may be 2.75%. This represented a reduction from the earlier requirement of 5%.
tq: Use the close numerical alternatives and distinguish the current figure from the earlier requirement.
sec: IPO process - book building, anchors, ASBA, SME IPO, listing

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the confidential pre-filing of a Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP)?
o: It permits an issuer to avoid filing any prospectus with the securities regulator
It allows a prospective issuer to submit the DRHP confidentially before the public issue process, as in the case of Razorpay
It enables anchor investors to keep their bids secret after allotment
It is a facility available only after the shares are listed
x: Confidential pre-filing of the DRHP is used before the public issue process. Razorpay is an example associated with this mechanism; it does not eliminate regulatory filing.
tq: Match the procedural facility with its stage and the stated example.
sec: IPO process - book building, anchors, ASBA, SME IPO, listing

s: In the context of the Budget 2026–27, the increase in Securities Transaction Tax (STT) on futures and options (F&O) was intended primarily to:
o: Curb speculation in the derivatives market
Provide interest subsidies to IPO applicants
Replace the Goods and Services Tax on equity trades
x: The STT hike on F&O in Budget 2026–27 was aimed at curbing speculation. It was not intended to subsidise IPO applications or replace GST.
tq: Link the fiscal measure to its stated policy objective rather than to an unrelated market function.

s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the position regarding short-tenure options in India?
o: SEBI is still studying losses associated with short-tenure options
SEBI has prohibited all short-tenure options permanently
Short-tenure options are issued only through SME platforms
The Reserve Bank of India has made short-tenure options compulsory for retail investors
x: SEBI is still studying losses associated with short-tenure options. The available information does not state that such options have been permanently prohibited or made compulsory.
tq: Watch for extreme words such as ‘all’ and ‘permanently’ in regulatory statements.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the change in the household equity share in financial savings?
o: It declined from 15.2% in FY12 to 2% in FY25
It remained unchanged at 2% between FY12 and FY25
It increased from 2% in FY12 to 15.2% in FY25
It increased from 5% in FY12 to 12% in FY25
x: Household equity participation in financial savings rose substantially, from 2% in FY12 to 15.2% in FY25.
tq: Read the direction of change first, then verify both the initial and final percentages.

s: The number of unique investors in India crossed which threshold according to the Economic Survey 2025–26?
x: The number of unique investors crossed 12 crore according to the Economic Survey 2025–26.
tq: Match the reported threshold with the closest numerical distractors.

s:
Arrange the following institutions or exchanges in the order indicated by their respective ‘first’ status:
A. India INX — first international exchange
B. NSDL — first depository
C. BSE — Asia’s oldest exchange

Choose the correct combination of statements.
x: BSE is Asia’s oldest exchange, NSDL was India’s first depository, and India INX was India’s first international exchange. Hence, all three statements are correct.
tq: Verify each institutional distinction separately before selecting the complete option.
